The Institute of The Spiritual Science of Human Patterns Brand directions · For review

Five doors into the same Institute.

Michael, your outline gives us the architecture: the Courses, the Concepts, the Schools, the Human Operating System. What it does not yet have is a room to sit in. A tone of voice, a set of colors, a way of setting type that tells someone within two seconds what kind of place this is.

Here are five. None is finished, and none is a recommendation you have to accept. They exist so you can point at something and say what feels right and what does not.

Prepared for

Michael Schwartz

Stage

Direction, before any build

Decision needed

One direction to develop

Fixed

The full Institute name, exactly as written

How to read this

  1. Scroll through all five before deciding anything. They are meant to be seen against one another, not judged one at a time.
  2. Each one is laid out the same way and in the same order, so you can compare like with like: archetype, promise, voice, sample lines, palette, type, imagery, interface, and our own honest read on where it wins and what it risks.
  3. Nothing here is finished, and nothing has been built. Tell Sara what feels right and what does not, in whatever form is easiest for you.

The photographs are directional. They show tone, color and texture, not final artwork.

Shared

What holds true in all five

The name

Nine words is a masthead, not a nav item. Every direction uses a stacked lockup that breaks the name across three lines and lets the type carry it, plus one short form for everything else.

  • FullMastheads, footers, certificates, book covers, anything legal.
  • Short"The Institute" in navigation, buttons, and body copy after first mention.
  • NeverAn acronym. ISSHP is unpronounceable and gives away the seriousness.
Nomenclature

You already capitalize your terms, and that instinct is right. Capitalization is what turns vocabulary into a discipline. It needs to become a written rule, because other people will write for this site eventually.

  • CapitalConcept, Pattern, Concept Family, Concept Weave, Pattern Weave, School, Foundation Course, Human Operating System.
  • LowerThe same words used ordinarily. A pattern in a carpet is not a Pattern.
  • ChainConcept, Belief, Pattern, Emotion, Behavior, Life Result. Always that order, always with arrows.
First screen

One sentence, one primary action, one secondary action. Everything else lives behind the accordions you described. A visitor should be able to start without believing they have missed something.

Never

Countdown timers, seat-scarcity language, before and after testimonials, stock photography of people meditating on beaches, chakra charts, mandalas used as wallpaper.

Direction A

The Quiet Room

A private writing room, painted rather than photographed. Your own writing, given somewhere to sit.

Archetype

Sage, with Caregiver underneath.

The Sage's authority comes from having looked carefully over a long time, not from having answers. The Caregiver underneath keeps it from going cold: the reader is never made to feel behind.

Promise

You will not be rushed, and you will not be graded.

Voice
  • Speak plainly about interior things.
    YesA Concept does not remain merely an idea. It expresses itself through behavior you can recognize.
    NoUnlock the hidden architecture of your soul.
  • Remove the pressure before extending the invitation.
    YesYou do not have to understand everything before you begin.
    NoEnrollment closes Friday. Only 40 seats remain.
  • Describe, do not diagnose.
    YesThirty Patterns that may influence how we think, choose, and respond.
    NoIdentify your unresolved abandonment wound.
  • Let sentences end.
    YesTen weeks. Thirty Patterns. Three at a time.
    NoA transformative journey of profound and lasting self-discovery that will change everything.

Imagery

Gilt-tooled emblem on oxblood leather, in lamplight.

Daylight variant. Same room, richer color.

  • Oil painting rather than photography. A commissioned or licensed set, or one painterly treatment applied consistently.
  • Interiors of rooms where somebody works alone. A desk, a window, shelves, a lamp.
  • One warm light source does the work. The rest of the room falls away into indigo and slate.
  • Visible brushwork where the light lands, thin and quiet in the darks.
  • Objects carry the meaning: bindings, brass, wax, wood, cloth, dried stems.
  • The mark belongs on things that are made: tooled into leather, stamped in foil, pressed into a cover. Not floating on a blank sheet.
  • No people in frame, and no faces anywhere in the system.
  • No stock photography, no flatlays, no styled desks, no hands holding mugs.
  • Where a photograph is unavoidable, it gets treated to sit beside the paintings rather than compete with them.
Interface

Generous margins and hairline brass rules. No drop shadows and no rounded cards; separation comes from space and rules. Accordions cross-fade open instead of sliding.

Our read

Where it wins

Closest to how you already write, so the copy you have drafted needs almost no rework. Ages well. Reads as an institution rather than a course platform.

What it risks

One palette slip toward terracotta and cream and it becomes a wellness brand. It is also the quietest of the five, so the Schools have to work to feel distinct from one another.

Direction B

The Inner Cosmos

A person with a cosmos inside them, and gold growing up around. There is a structure underneath, and it can be drawn.

Archetype

Magician, with Sage underneath.

The Magician here is the archetype of transformation through understanding: the power comes from seeing an order that was already operating. The Sage underneath keeps it from drifting into mysticism, because everything claimed here gets explained.

Promise

There is a structure underneath, and it can be seen.

Voice
  • Lead with the question, then the mechanism.
    YesWhy can we consciously want one thing and repeatedly create something different?
    NoDiscover your authentic self.
  • Treat the system as real and describable.
    YesConcept to Belief to Pattern to Emotion to Behavior to Life Result. Drawn once, referred back to.
    NoEverything is connected in ways we cannot fully know.
  • Reverence without incense.
    YesAwe from scale and precision.
    NoAncient wisdom the modern world has forgotten.
  • Draw it before you write it.
    YesFamilies, Weaves, and the Operating System get diagrams first.
    NoThree paragraphs describing a relationship a single diagram would show.

Explore the Human Operating System

Imagery

Head and shoulders variant of the mark.

Gold botanical linework, engraved not illustrated.

  • The figure is the mark: a human outline in a single hairline, holding a cosmos inside it.
  • Gold botanical linework grows around and through the figure. Engraved, not illustrated.
  • Inside the outline is deep space. Outside it is near-black and mostly empty.
  • One figure per page. It is a statement, not a pattern to be tiled.
  • Diagrams use the same hairline gold, so the Weaves and the Operating System belong to the same drawing.
  • Light entering dark architecture stays available for interior pages, in the same palette.
  • No faces, no features, no anatomical detail. The outline is enough.
  • No nebula photographs as wallpaper, and no chakra points marked on the body.
Interface

Dark by default and it stays dark. Content fades up as though being lit. Each diagram draws itself once on first view, then holds still. Progress through a School shown as points on a line rather than a percentage bar.

Our read

Where it wins

The only direction that makes the Human Operating System and the Weaves genuinely legible, and those are the hardest and most valuable ideas you have. Nothing else in this category looks like it.

What it risks

Dark grounds tire the eye over long study sessions, so course reading may need a lighter surface inside the dark shell. If the gold gets ornate it tips into new age.

Explore Concept Families

Imagery

Vein structure. Pattern found rather than drawn.

Blind-embossed mark, moss and ochre in limestone paper.

  • Pattern found in nature at close range. Veins, roots, sand, water rings, stone, bark, seed heads.
  • Overhead and macro. The pattern fills the frame edge to edge.
  • Natural light only, and light that has travelled: late afternoon, through a leaf, off water.
  • Hands are permitted when they are doing something. Faces are not.
  • One subject per image. A pattern needs room to be read.
  • Nothing arranged. Found rather than styled.
  • Where the mark appears on a made object, the surface stays earthen: handmade paper, unglazed clay, undyed cloth.
  • No lifestyle photography, no yoga mats, no soft-focus sun through leaves, no candles.
Interface

Softened edges without rounded cards. Sections separated by a shift in ground texture rather than boxes. Course progress drawn as ten marks that fill in, so a student sees the shape of the whole before starting.

Our read

Where it wins

Warmest and most approachable, and the easiest to sustain across email and social where the others get stiff. Natural home for the Foundation Course and the School of the Symbolic Body.

What it risks

Closest to the crowded wellness category, and the palette gives up some of the seriousness the name is claiming. The type has to carry it.

Direction D

The Golden Ratio

The moment the pattern becomes visible. Light, proportion, and geometry that were there the whole time.

Archetype

Magician, with Innocent underneath.

Where B is the Magician as precise revealer, this is the Magician as wonder. The Innocent underneath is the belief that the order is fundamentally good and that anyone can be shown it. That is why this direction is warm where B is austere.

Promise

The order was always there. Learning to see it is the beautiful part.

Voice
  • Let wonder do the work an argument would do.
    YesThe same proportion is in a shell, in a galaxy, and in the way a Pattern repeats.
    NoStudies show that sacred geometry improves wellbeing.
  • Beauty is the argument, so do not explain it.
    YesShort lines with a great deal of space around them.
    NoA paragraph justifying why the site looks the way it does.
  • Warm rather than cool. The universe here is friendly.
    YesYou are already inside the pattern. This is about noticing it.
    NoThe self is an illusion generated by conditioned response.
  • Every mystical word has to be one of yours.
    YesConcept, Pattern, Weave, Human Operating System, the Five Laws.
    NoVibration, frequency, quantum, high-dimensional energy.

Interface · Manrope

Start the free course

Imagery

Fibonacci study. Hairline gold on a violet field.

Gradient field. One per surface, never two.

  • Luminous geometry over gradient fields. Seed of Life, Flower of Life, Fibonacci, in hairline gold.
  • Gradients travel from violet through magenta into amber. One per surface, never two competing.
  • The geometry is drawn properly. Correct circles, correct proportions, no approximations.
  • Light blooms where the lines cross. That is the only glow effect in the system.
  • Stars used as punctuation, a handful at most. Never a full starfield.
  • Where photography is used at all, it is real sky and real light, not composited space art.
  • No third eyes, no lotus flowers, no crystals, no rainbow chakra columns, no purple-to-blue tech gradients.
Interface

Gradients are grounds, never buttons. Geometry appears once per page, large and low in opacity behind the content. A lavender tint carries secondary text so the violet stays readable. Course reading happens on a calm dark surface, not on a gradient.

Our read

Where it wins

Exactly the cosmic, colorful look, and the warmest of all five. It photographs beautifully for social and email, and it gives your more mystical material permission to look mystical instead of apologizing for itself.

What it risks

The most crowded look in this category by a wide margin, and gradients date faster than anything else on this page. It survives only on restraint: one geometry per page, one gradient per surface, and the vocabulary rule above held strictly. It is also the hardest of the five to keep readable across fifty Concept pages.

Direction E

The Illuminated Book

A treatise someone copied out by hand because it mattered enough to.

Archetype

Sage, with Magician underneath.

The scholar-mystic. Authority comes from a long tradition of careful record: this was studied, argued over, and written down by people who took it seriously. The Magician underneath is what keeps it from being merely academic.

Promise

This has been studied for a long time, and set down carefully.

Voice
  • Write as though it will be read in fifty years.
    YesEverything begins with Concept.
    NoHere's the thing about patterns.
  • Let the structure show.
    YesThe Second Law. Book Two, on Identity.
    NoModule 4: Deep Dive.
  • Use the margin for warmth. The main text stays formal.
    YesA marginal note reading: most students recognize this one immediately.
    NoAn exclamation mark in the main text.
  • Modern English, old bearing. Never costume the language.
    YesThe purpose is not to judge or label.
    NoHerein lieth the wisdom of the ancients.

Interface · Marcellus

Enter the School of Identity

Imagery

Inked diagram on vellum. Vermilion, iron gall, gold leaf.

  • Hand-drawn on aged surfaces. Iron gall ink, vermilion and gold leaf, on vellum or laid paper.
  • Geometric diagrams sit in the margin, where a real treatise would put them.
  • Marginalia is part of the design: notes, pointing hands, small corrections left visible.
  • One illuminated initial per opening, and nowhere else on the page.
  • Botanical borders used once, as an event, never repeated as a frame.
  • Photograph the real thing under raking light so the surface reads. Flat scans lose it.
  • No fake distressing, no torn-paper overlays, no sepia filters, no wizards or scrolls.
Interface

Two columns where the content allows, with real marginal notes instead of tooltips. Rubricated headings in vermilion. One illuminated initial per Course opener and never more than one. Progress shown as a bookmark rather than a bar.

Our read

Where it wins

Nothing in this category looks like it, and it makes Institute, Schools, and Books & Study Editions read as one idea instead of three. It handles your written editions natively, and it is the most credible answer to the question of whether this is serious.

What it risks

It can slip into costume, which kills it instantly. The manuscript feeling has to come from structure and restraint rather than texture overlays. Small type on vellum is a real legibility problem that has to be solved at the start, and it is the hardest of the five to carry into email and social.

After this

What happens next

One direction, then a real specification.

Once you pick, that direction gets built out properly: the full name lockup, a mark, the type and color decisions written down as a spec, and a set of page layouts for the shapes the site actually needs. The Concept page, the Course page, the School page, the Weave diagram.

Nothing gets built against a direction until you have signed off on it, so there is no cost to changing your mind now and real cost to changing it later.

Still needed
  • Final course titles, and the titles of the Five Laws.
  • The complete Concept library, and which Families ship as standalone courses.
  • Whether "The Institute" works as the short form in navigation.
  • Any marks, seals, colors, or book covers from earlier materials, so we are not designing over something you already love.
  • Whether students receive anything printed. Certificates and workbooks change how the palette has to be built.
